output.brief:
The rise in delayed alarm responses most likely comes from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency nurses. The new server imported only 3 of 14 forwarding rules. The 11 skipped rules included the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, repeat-alarm suppression, and routing of probe-off alarms to the charge phone only. The import warned about this but reported success, and the smoke test checked only two beds. Pods A–C then went from about 38 to about 82 phone notifications per nurse per shift, and acknowledgement time roughly doubled. Pod D was not migrated and shows no change. Core, agency and agency-share groups all worsened equally in Pods A–C, and Pod D has the same agency share with no rise. Monitor alarm volume was flat, which counts against acuity and the monitor software update as causes. Alarm fatigue is the likely mechanism. Sick leave is a possible knock-on effect, but that link is not established.

Do not approve the agency cap or the performance reviews. They would punish the wrong party. Do not stop phone forwarding of SpO2 alarms either. Instead, restore the old rules (about 4 hours plus clinical validation), then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Confidence is high.
